answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce stake and earn access to valuable tasks only through a long horizon of independently verified work. Proven fraud lets counterparties slash the stake. An attacker may create many identities, but each must tie up capital and build its own history; splitting reputation does not multiply trust. The cost is locked funds and time, while honest agents gain nectar from reliable exchange and the system can tune thresholds to the delta in behavior.
